text: A genuinely dedicated workspace, a real publish, a working dashboard, and a fully packaged app — four real steps, and every single one of them already familiar to you directly from Chapter Nine's coverage of the Power BI service.

Create a workspace set up specifically just for this one project, something like Adventure Works Sales Capstone, rather than reusing a workspace from an earlier chapter's lab. Publish straight from Desktop into it, then open the published report in the service and confirm every single page — including that hidden drillthrough page — genuinely renders correctly with real data populating every visual.

A dashboard pinning exactly one tile from each of the three report pages gives the VP a genuinely real at-a-glance view of everything that matters most, with every single tile still linking straight back to its own full report page for anyone who wants deeper detail behind the headline.

Package the whole thing up as a real app, following the same three-tab flow from Lesson 73: give it a proper name and description on Setup, add both the report and the dashboard you just built as Content, then create one single audience group under Audience, and publish the entire thing live.

Being published doesn't automatically mean it's actually shared with the right people yet, and it genuinely doesn't mean it'll stay current once real underlying data starts changing. Lesson 92 covers both of those separately and deliberately, one careful step at a time.
